title.en: The dative case: to whom, and how it feels

card: The dative is the ***to/for*** case: the person something is given, said or shown to: **Я дал бра́ту кни́гу.** It also marks who *experiences* a feeling or state: **Мне хо́лодно** (*I'm cold*), **Мне нра́вится** (*I like*), and follows **к** (*towards*) and **по** (*along, by*). Singular endings: **-у/-ю** (masc./neut.), **-е** (fem. **-а/-я**), **-и** (fem. **-ь**).

sections.body: The dative is the case of the *receiver*. Whoever ends up with the gift, the message or the feeling goes in the dative. That is why it appears in Russian's many "impersonal" phrases: instead of *I am cold*, Russian says *to-me it is cold*, **мне хо́лодно**, because the person is treated as the one who experiences the cold, not the one who does something.

sections.title: The main uses
sections.body:
- **Indirect object** with verbs of giving and telling: **дать**, **дари́ть**, **сказа́ть**, **писа́ть**, **звони́ть**, **показа́ть**, **объясни́ть**: **Позвони́ ма́ме!**
- **Verbs that take the dative where English uses an object**: **помога́ть** (*help*), **меша́ть** (*disturb*), **сове́товать** (*advise*), **ве́рить** (*believe*): **Я помога́ю дру́гу.**
- **Feelings and states** with an adverb in **-о**: **мне хо́лодно / ску́чно / интере́сно / ве́село**.
- **Liking**: **Мне нра́вится му́зыка.** The thing liked is the *subject*; you are the dative receiver.
- **Need and permission**: **мне на́до / ну́жно**, **мне мо́жно**, **мне нельзя́**.
- **Age**: **Мне два́дцать лет.** (*To me are twenty years.*)
- **Prepositions**: **к** (*towards, to someone's place*): **Я иду́ к врачу́**; **по** (*along, around, by means of*): **по у́лице**, **по телефо́ну**.

English *I like music* puts *I* first as the subject. Russian turns it round: **Мне нра́вится му́зыка**, *music pleases me*. So the verb agrees with the music, not with you: **Мне нра́вятся э́ти пе́сни** (*I like these songs*). Think of the Spanish *me gusta* if you know it.
Picture a hand reaching out to receive: whoever's hand it is, that word goes in the dative. *Give **him** the book*, *tell **Mum**, it's cold **to me***: all hands.

mistakes.why: The person who likes is in the dative; the thing liked is the subject.
**помога́ть** takes the dative, not the accusative.
States and feelings use the dative of the person, with no subject.
